attribution.note: Marcus writes in his own voice that he very much agrees with the AG's position. That explicit endorsement makes the proposition his claim, not just a quotation.

semantics.note: The normalisation matches his words. It is phrased as a present-tense observation, but 'properly' makes it an evaluative judgment with no stated test, so it is untestable as written.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats 'properly regulate' as a normative standard with no measure. It does not invent a test, and so it declines to grade, which is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: Florida Phoenix report from 2026-09-28. It shows the position is an AG allegation in pending litigation, not a court or regulator finding.
OpenAI spokesperson statement on pausing training of its most capable models. This is a company disclosure, and it can be read either way, so it does not settle the normative question.
Help Net Security, August 2026. It reports a containment incident and OpenAI's own remedial controls. This is relevant background but not a test of 'proper' self-regulation.

reviews.rationale: Marcus endorses the claim that OpenAI cannot 'properly' regulate its own tech. That is an evaluative judgment with no measure or threshold. No court or independent audit had ruled by the cutoff, and the incident and pause evidence can be read both ways. The claim is untestable as stated, so it is not graded.
